filters.name: Sample Mesh Elements
filters.shortDescription: Create a point set by subsampling mesh vertices, edges, or faces.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Create a new layer holding one sample per mesh element. **Number of samples** elements are drawn uniformly at random -- every element of the chosen kind is equally likely -- and one point is emitted for each: a **Vertex** contributes its own position, an **Edge** its midpoint, a **Face** its barycenter. Asking for at least as many samples as there are elements simply returns them all.

Edge sampling ignores *faux* edges, the diagonals that triangulate a polygonal face, since those are not edges of the polygonal mesh and the wireframe does not draw them. Note that midpoints and barycenters lie slightly inside a curved surface, which is inherent to taking a single sample per element. To place several samples along each edge instead, in proportion to its length, use *Sample Surface by Stratified Triangles* with the **Sample Edges** strategy.

parameters.label: Element to sample
parameters.help: Choose which mesh elements are sampled.

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: How many elements to draw. Reaching or exceeding the element count returns every element.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the chosen subset of elements exactly reproducible. It has no effect when the requested number reaches the element count, since then every element is taken.

filters.name: Sample Surface by Monte Carlo
filters.shortDescription: Create a random point cloud from the current surface.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a new layer populated with a point sampling of the current mesh; samples are generated in a randomly uniform way, or with a distribution biased by the per-vertex quality values of the mesh.

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: Desired number of generated samples.

parameters.label: Quality Weighted Sampling
parameters.help: Use per-vertex quality to bias the sampling density.

parameters.label: Per-Face Normal
parameters.help: Store the face normal on each sample instead of interpolated vertex normals.

parameters.label: Radius Variance
parameters.help: When quality-weighted sampling is used, the sampling radius may vary between r/var and r*var.

parameters.label: Exact Sample Number
parameters.help: If enabled, try to generate exactly the requested number of samples.

parameters.label: Sample Crease Edges Only
parameters.help: Restrict sampling to mesh edges.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the sample positions exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Sample Surface by Stratified Triangles
filters.shortDescription: Generate structured samples over the triangle mesh.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a new layer populated with a point sampling of the current mesh; to generate multiple samples inside a triangle each triangle is subdivided according to various stratified strategies. Distribution is often biased by triangle shape.

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: Desired number of generated samples.

parameters.label: Sampling strategy
parameters.help: Choose the structured sampling strategy.

parameters.label: Random Sampling
parameters.help: For each virtual cell, choose a random sample instead of the midpoint.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the sample positions inside each face exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Sample Vertices by Clustering
filters.shortDescription: Cluster the point set into grid cells and keep one representative per cell.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a new layer populated with a subsampling of the vertices of the current mesh; the subsampling is driven by a simple one-per-gridded cell strategy.

parameters.label: Cell Size
parameters.help: Size of the clustering grid cell. Smaller cells preserve more detail.

parameters.label: Representative Strategy
parameters.help: Choose how each cell representative is computed.

parameters.label: Only on Selection
parameters.help: If enabled, use only the selected subset of the mesh as input.

filters.name: Sample Surface by Poisson Disk
filters.shortDescription: Generate well-spaced samples over a surface or point cloud.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Create a new layer populated with a point sampling of the current mesh;samples are generated according to a Poisson-disk distribution, using the algorithm described in:
'Efficient and Flexible Sampling with Blue Noise Properties of Triangular Meshes'
Massimiliano Corsini, Paolo Cignoni, Roberto Scopigno
IEEE TVCG 2012

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: Desired number of samples. Ignored if an explicit radius is provided.

parameters.label: Explicit Radius
parameters.help: If non-zero, overrides the sample number and uses this radius directly.

parameters.label: Montecarlo Oversampling
parameters.help: Oversampling factor used to generate the initial Montecarlo candidates.

parameters.label: Save Montecarlo
parameters.help: Also create a layer containing the raw Montecarlo candidates.

parameters.label: Approximate Geodesic Distance
parameters.help: Use a normal-aware approximate geodesic distance during Poisson pruning.

parameters.label: Base Mesh Subsampling
parameters.help: Use the original vertices as the candidate set instead of generating Montecarlo samples.

parameters.label: Refine Existing Samples
parameters.help: Use an existing sample layer as pre-generated seeds that are refined further.

parameters.label: Samples to refine
parameters.help: Layer used as the initial sample set when Refine Existing Samples is enabled.

parameters.label: Best Sample Heuristic
parameters.help: Use a heuristic to improve the maximality of the chosen sample set.

parameters.label: Best Sample Pool Size
parameters.help: Number of candidate attempts used when the best-sample heuristic is enabled.

parameters.label: Precise Sample Number
parameters.help: Search for a radius that matches the requested number of samples within the given tolerance.

parameters.label: Precise Sample Tolerance
parameters.help: Tolerance used by precise sample count search, expressed as a fraction of the requested sample count.

parameters.label: Radius Variance
parameters.help: Allow the Poisson disk radius to vary between r and r*var using vertex quality as a density bias.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the generated sample set exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Measure Hausdorff Distance
filters.shortDescription: Compute directional Hausdorff distance statistics between two meshes.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute the Measure Hausdorff Distance between two layers, sampling one of the two and finding for each sample the closest point over the other mesh. If sample layers are saved, distances are stored in vertex quality and MeshLab switches those layers to vertex-quality color visualization without baking colors.

parameters.label: Sampled mesh
parameters.help: The mesh whose surface is sampled.

parameters.label: Target mesh
parameters.help: The reference mesh searched for closest points.

parameters.label: Save Samples
parameters.help: Create two new layers with the used sample points and closest points.

parameters.label: Sample Vertices
parameters.help: Sample vertices of the sampled mesh.

parameters.label: Sample Edges
parameters.help: Sample edges of the sampled mesh.

parameters.label: Sample Faux Edges
parameters.help: Include faux edges when edge sampling is enabled.

parameters.label: Sample Faces
parameters.help: Sample faces of the sampled mesh by Montecarlo sampling.

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: Desired number of samples for each enabled sampling strategy.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.help: Discard sample points whose closest point is farther than this threshold.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the measured sample set exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Compute Distance from Reference Mesh
filters.shortDescription: Compute per-vertex distance from another mesh or point cloud.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute the signed/unsigned (per vertex) distance between a mesh/pointcloud and a reference mesh/pointcloud. Distance is stored in vertex quality; after the filter runs MeshLab switches the measured mesh to vertex-quality color visualization without baking colors.

parameters.label: Measured mesh
parameters.help: The mesh that will receive the computed distances in vertex quality.

parameters.label: Reference mesh
parameters.help: The mesh or point cloud used as the reference.

parameters.label: Compute Signed Distance
parameters.help: If enabled, compute a signed distance instead of the absolute value.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.help: Search is interrupted when nothing is found within this range.

filters.name: Sample Texels
filters.shortDescription: Create one point sample per covered texel in texture space.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Create a new layer with a point sampling of the current mesh, a sample for each texel of the mesh is generated

parameters.label: Texture Width
parameters.help: Sampling resolution in texels. If 0 and Recover Color is enabled, use the current texture width.

parameters.label: Texture Height
parameters.help: Sampling resolution in texels. If 0 and Recover Color is enabled, use the current texture height.

parameters.label: UV Space Sampling
parameters.help: Place output points in UV space instead of the original mesh space.

parameters.label: Recover Color
parameters.help: Sample the current texture image and store its colors on the generated points.

parameters.label: Source Texture
parameters.help: When Recover Color is enabled, choose which associated texture to sample. Automatic uses each face's per-wedge texture slot assignment.

filters.name: Transfer Vertex Attributes by Closest Point
filters.shortDescription: Transfer attributes from one mesh to another by closest-point projection.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Transfer the chosen per-vertex attributes from one layer to another. Useful to transfer attributes to different representations of a same object.
For each vertex of the target mesh the closest point (not vertex!) on the source mesh is computed, and the requested interpolated attributes from that source point are copied into the target vertex.
The algorithm assumes that the two meshes are reasonably similar and aligned.

parameters.label: Source mesh
parameters.help: The mesh that provides the attributes to transfer.

parameters.label: Target mesh
parameters.help: The mesh whose vertices receive the transferred attributes.

parameters.label: Vertex Sampling
parameters.help: If enabled, transfer attributes from the closest source vertex instead of the closest point on the source surface.

parameters.label: Transfer Geometry
parameters.help: Snap target vertices onto the corresponding closest point on the source.

parameters.label: Transfer Normal
parameters.help: Transfer interpolated normals from the source.

parameters.label: Transfer Color
parameters.help: Transfer vertex colors from the source.

parameters.label: Transfer Quality
parameters.help: Transfer vertex quality from the source.

parameters.label: Transfer Selection
parameters.help: Select target vertices whose corresponding closest point lies on selected source elements.

parameters.label: Store Distance as Quality
parameters.help: Store the transfer distance in the target vertex quality.

parameters.label: Save Barycentric Coords
parameters.help: Store barycentric coordinates and nearest face or vertex indices as per-vertex attributes on the target mesh.

parameters.label: Max Dist Search
parameters.help: Closest-point searches farther than this threshold are rejected.

parameters.label: Only on Selection
parameters.help: If enabled, transfer only to selected target vertices.

filters.name: Remesh Uniformly by Volumetric Resampling
filters.shortDescription: Build an offset mesh from a signed distance field sampled on a regular grid.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Create a new mesh that is a resampled version of the current one.
The resampling is done by building a uniform volumetric representation where each voxel contains the signed distance from the original surface. The resampled surface is reconstructed using the marching cube algorithm over this volume.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.help: Sampling cell size. Smaller cells give more precise results at higher cost.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: Offset of the extracted surface relative to the original mesh.

parameters.label: Clean Vertices
parameters.help: Merge nearly coincident vertices in the generated mesh.

parameters.label: Discretize
parameters.help: Use fixed edge midpoints instead of linear interpolation for a stair-step appearance.

parameters.label: Multi-sample
parameters.help: Compute the distance field more accurately by multisampling the volume.

parameters.label: Absolute Distance
parameters.help: Use an unsigned distance field to create an inner and outer shell around the input mesh.

filters.name: Colorize Vertices by Voronoi Regions
filters.shortDescription: Color a mesh according to projected seed points from another layer.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Given a Mesh M and a Pointset P, The filter project each vertex of P over M and color M according to the geodesic distance from these projected points. Projection and coloring are done on a per vertex basis.

parameters.label: To be colored mesh
parameters.help: The mesh whose surface will be colored.

parameters.label: Vertex mesh
parameters.help: The point cloud whose vertices are used as Voronoi seeds.

parameters.label: BackDistance
parameters.help: Color according to the distance from the Voronoi frontier instead of from the seed.

filters.name: Colorize Vertices by Disk Distance
filters.shortDescription: Color a mesh according to the distance from projected point-cloud disks.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Given a Mesh M and a Pointset P, The filter project each vertex of P over M and color M according to the Euclidean distance from these projected points. Projection and coloring are done on a per vertex basis.

parameters.label: To be colored mesh
parameters.help: The mesh whose vertices will be colored.

parameters.label: Vertex mesh
parameters.help: The point cloud whose vertices are used as disk centers.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.help: Disk radius around each point-cloud seed.

parameters.label: Use sample radius
parameters.help: Use the per-vertex quality of the seed cloud as the disk radius.

parameters.label: Use Approximate Geodetic
parameters.help: Weight the Euclidean distance by the normal difference between the two points.

filters.name: Sample Offset Surface Recursively
filters.shortDescription: Generate offset surface samples by recursively subdividing the bounding box.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: The bounding box is recursively partitioned in a octree style, center of bbox are considered, when the center is nearer to the surface than a given threshold it is projected on it. It works also for building offsetted samples.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.help: Subdivision threshold. Smaller values generate denser samples.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: Offset distance applied to the projected samples.

filters.name: Simplify Point Cloud
filters.shortDescription: Simplify a point cloud with Poisson-disk pruning.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Create a new layer populated with a simplified version of the current point cloud. The simplification is performed by subsampling the original point cloud using a Poisson Disk strategy using the algorithm described in:
'Efficient and Flexible Sampling with Blue Noise Properties of Triangular Meshes'
Massimiliano Corsini, Paolo Cignoni, Roberto Scopigno
IEEE TVCG 2012

parameters.label: Number of samples
parameters.help: Desired number of samples. Ignored if an explicit radius is provided.

parameters.label: Explicit Radius
parameters.help: If non-zero, overrides the sample number and uses this radius directly.

parameters.label: Best Sample Heuristic
parameters.help: Use a heuristic to improve the maximality of the chosen sample set.

parameters.label: Best Sample Pool Size
parameters.help: Number of candidate attempts used when the best-sample heuristic is enabled.

parameters.label: Precise Sample Number
parameters.help: Search for a radius that matches the requested number of samples within the given tolerance.

parameters.label: Precise Sample Tolerance
parameters.help: Tolerance used by precise sample count search, expressed as a fraction of the requested sample count.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the surviving subset of points exactly reproducible.
